questions.q: What does ON 100 PERCENT DO SUSPEND actually do on driftwood_etl_monitor?
options: Stops the warehouse from accepting new queries once its credit quota is fully consumed
Sends a Slack notification with no other effect
Automatically increases the credit quota by 100%
Deletes the warehouse entirely
questions.explain: DO SUSPEND is the real guardrail -- the warehouse stops running new queries, preventing a runaway cost from continuing past the budget.

questions.q: What real failure shape does retries=1 with a 10-minute delay handle in the Airflow DAG?
options: A transient Snowflake connection hiccup that succeeds on a second attempt, without paging anyone unnecessarily
A permanent data quality bug in the source files
A Terraform state lock conflict
A Power BI refresh failure
questions.explain: A single retry with a short delay is specifically sized to absorb transient issues, not mask a genuine persistent failure, which still triggers on_failure_callback after retries are exhausted.

questions.q: Why does on_failure_callback matter for trust in the dashboard, specifically?
options: It alerts the data team the same morning a run fails, before leadership opens a dashboard built on stale or half-built data without anyone knowing
It automatically fixes the failed task without human intervention
It prevents the DAG from ever failing again
It only matters for reducing Snowflake compute costs
questions.explain: The real risk without this alert is a silent failure -- leadership trusting a number built on stale or incomplete data with no indication anything went wrong.

questions.q: What is the recommended troubleshooting order when a stakeholder reports "the MRR number looks off"?
options: Check the Airflow run status first, then dbt test results, then Snowflake query history -- before suspecting the DAX measure itself
Immediately rewrite the DAX measure from scratch
Check the DAX measure first, since that's where numbers are calculated
Restart the entire pipeline from the beginning without investigating
questions.explain: Following the pipeline's own dependency order finds the real cause faster than guessing -- the DAX measure logic is usually the least likely culprit once the pipeline's own correctness is confirmed.

questions.q: Why is the resource monitor's 50-credit quota described as "deliberately generous" for a once-daily batch job?
options: The point isn't constraining normal operation -- it's catching the specific failure mode of a runaway query or a forgotten auto-resumed warehouse before it becomes a cost surprise
50 credits is the minimum value Snowflake allows for a resource monitor
A generous quota means the monitor will never actually trigger
It's set high specifically to allow unlimited ad hoc analyst queries
questions.explain: The quota is a guardrail against a specific abnormal failure mode, not a tight operational constraint on expected daily usage.
